create.name: Ramakrishna Vedanta Society of North Texas
create.bio:
The Ramakrishna Vedanta Society of North Texas is a centre of the Ramakrishna Order in Irving, Texas, serving people across the Dallas-Fort Worth area. Monks of the order had visited and lectured there since the 1960s, and devotees later hosted retreats in their homes; with the encouragement of Swami Swahananda of the Vedanta Society of Southern California, the society was registered in 2006 and opened its monastery and chapel, a converted garden shed, in a house in Irving the following year. A resident minister lives at the monastery, and visiting swamis and nuns lead retreats through the year.

Its teaching follows Sri Ramakrishna, Sarada Devi and Swami Vivekananda, presented through the four yogas of service, knowledge, devotion and meditation, and all programmes are in English, open to everyone and funded by donations. The YouTube channel, active since 2018, carries Sunday lectures, retreat sessions and multi-part study classes on texts such as the Taittiriya Upanishad and the Narada Bhakti Sutra, given by resident and guest monastics including Swami Sarvapriyananda, alongside recordings of festivals.

www.vedantadfw.org serves no robots.txt (404), so no rules apply.

Swami Sarvapriyananda (listed as part of the Vedanta Society of New York) appears as a guest speaker on this channel; a video is not evidence of teaching there, so no teacher links. Teachers file has no links.
Thin on site items: one free-resource page, no offerings (programmes are free and donation-funded); videos carry the listing.
Photo is the channel avatar (a painted swan on water above a lotus with Om), used as the society's logo.
